newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia peacekeeper dies guarding election site.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia peacekeeper dies guarding election site.

text.p: A soldier in Bosnia's NATO-led peace force died of a gunshot wound on Sunday while guarding a Sarajevo warehouse filled with voting materials for next weekend's elections, international officials said.

The Ukrainian soldier was pronounced dead half an hour after the early-morning shooting outside the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) warehouse but initial reports of how it happened were confused.
OSCE spokesman Thomas Leary said its officials were told at the scene that three unidentified people approached the warehouse and shot the Ukrainian in a close-range ambush.
"Our report is that the Ukrainians returned fire but we don't know if anyone was hit," he said.
But Ukrainian soldiers at the warehouse had another story. They told Reuters their comrade "died inside his APC" (armoured personnel carrier), suggesting he might have shot himself.
Leary said the peace Implementation Force (IFOR) was taking the lead in the investigation.
NATO said the 12.30 a.m. (2230 GMT) incident occurred after the Ukrainians lit the warehouse area with a searchlight from their armoured vehicle to check out indications of intruders.

"One Ukrainian soldier was shot by a so-far unidentified person," IFOR's Major Simon Haselock said. "He was evacuated to IFOR's hospital at (nearby) Rajlovac where he was pronounced dead a half hour later."
The Ukrainian's identity was being withheld pending notification of his family.
Haselock said the two other Ukrainian soldiers were not injured in the incident and no assailants were apprehended.
He said IFOR could not confirm the Ukrainian was shot by someone trying to break into the warehouse but an investigation was under way to clarify the circumstances.
"A thorough search of the area around the warehouse by IFOR military police for some clues...began immediately after the shooting and continues today," Haselock said.

Leary said nothing appeared to have been stolen or disturbed in the warehouse, which contains ballot papers and other materials for Bosnia's first post-war elections next Saturday, supervised by the OSCE.
